name: pipepair
algorithm: one process makes an anonymous pipe; a second task (thread, goroutine) writes n bytes to the write end in 64 KiB writes, one 64 KiB chunk of a splitmix64 stream (each word's 8 bytes little endian, from state 0) filled once and written again and again, then closes it; the main task reads the read end into a 64 KiB buffer, sums the bytes and prints the bytes read and their sum (tests/bench-lanes/std-proc3/README.md).
notes: Written by std-proc3 (status/std-proc3.md, review P3X-5) over the public proc.Pipe, PipeWriter.WriteAll and PipeReader.Read: both ends are proc.Pipe's, which the runtime reads and writes on its blocking pool (P3R-1, request 17). Go is os.Pipe with a goroutine, Rust std::io::pipe with a thread.

skip.c: no std facility: ISO C has no pipes or threads of this kind (pipe and CreatePipe are OS APIs, not the C library)
skip.zig: no anonymous pipe on Windows in Zig 0.17's standard library: std.Io has pipe2 for POSIX targets only, and a CreatePipe call would be the program's own Windows binding, not the library's
